The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has advised Nigerians residing in the United Kingdom to stop sending money to people who seek financial help at home. Obi also advised them to urge their relatives to vote for productive leaders. He made the remarks at a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester, United Kingdom, on Sunday. He stressed that Nigeria’s prevailing economic hardship resulted from bad leadership, arguing that continuous financial assistance only cushions the effects of poor governance without addressing the root causes. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” he said. No governor has done it. “Let’s start with this one that is less corrupt. That’s how other countries change.” He maintained that his conversations with the people reinforced the need for collective responsibility, stressing that building a new Nigeria would require citizens to take an active role in addressing challenges facing the country. Obi also urged Nigerians to take the 2027 election seriously, describing the contest as a critical moment for the nation.
